decisions.reason: The complete-moment and teaching-value language restates the candidate's existing standard; selecting music to fit the mood does not change narrative completeness.
The request for clean editing does not add to or alter the existing clean, simple, professional visual-editing standard, and the music-selection change has no necessary visual-editing effect.
Using B-roll naturally restates the existing integration rule; requiring mood-appropriate music does not modify B-roll behavior.
The source message does not change the permitted source collection or source-exclusion rule; the music-selection decision is independent.
White text only restates the current white-text standard, while the mood-based music requirement does not change caption color or effects.
The source message does not discuss or alter the required caption font.
Neither the mood-based music change nor the other clauses in the source message modify hook selection or hook quality.
The instruction that each clip teach something real restates the existing requirement to select substantive lessons, stories, or real points; the music change adds no further moment-selection rule.
The twelve-clip launch batch was already current before message 191, so the source repeats rather than changes the assigned batch.
References to approved clips being posted are consistent with the existing approval-gated publishing rule and do not change its authority or condition.
The 70-to-85-second range exactly restates the candidate's current duration bounds.
Message 191 concerns the current twelve-clip launch batch and mood-appropriate music, not the deferred monthly target or its approval-counting rules.
